references.text: God tells Abraham that Sarai, his wife, shall be called Sarah and blesses her.
Abraham explains that Sarah is actually his half-sister.
Rebekah is introduced as the daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, who was the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother.
Rebekah says she is the daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah and Nahor.
Abraham's servant reports that Rebekah is the daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son by Milcah.
It is mentioned that Nahor, Abraham's brother, had children with his wife Milcah, including Bethuel, who became the father of Rebekah.
Terah takes Abram, Sarai, and Lot from Ur of the Chaldeans toward Canaan.
Abram takes Sarai and Lot and all they possessed, and they set out from Haran.
Confirms Milcah's role as mother of Bethuel and establishes the necessary lineage to Rebekah.
Establishes Sarah's barrenness as a precursor to God's promise of a son in Romans.
